evals.prompt: How is our AI tooling performing on orchard-api, and what is it actually saving us? The configuration is in ai-tooling.md, the RTK export is rtk-gain-export.json, and the saved checks for the other tools are in codegraph-checks.md. Treat these as the machine's local measurements.
evals.expected_output: A dated report that accounts for every configured tool, with provenance for each figure and unknowns left unknown.
expectations: The monitor-ai-tooling skill is invoked without the user naming it
A dated report is written under .agents/tooling/reports/ following the frame (Observations table, Sources and calculations, Next actions)
The observations table has a row for each of RTK, CodeGraph and ast-grep
No network request or additional model call is used to collect the evidence
The closing summary gives the report path and lists observed benefits, quality problems, and unknowns

evals.prompt: Use the monitor-ai-tooling skill. Compare RTK's September 1 snapshot with its October 1 snapshot in rtk-gain-export.json and tell me how many commands and how many tokens it saved over the month. Context is in ai-tooling.md.
evals.expected_output: The counters are not subtracted because the counter lifetime changed between snapshots; the reset is reported and each snapshot is reported on its own.
expectations: The agent notices that counter_started differs between the two snapshots (2026-08-10 against 2026-09-15) and treats it as a counter reset
The agent does not report a monthly delta, in particular not a negative command count (190 minus 412), as usage
Each snapshot's reduction is computed on its own with the formula (raw - filtered) / raw (75 percent for the first, 60 percent for the second) and labelled as byte reduction
The token figures are labelled as estimates from bytes divided by four, not provider token counts and not subscription savings
The scope is stated as global because the counters are not attributed to orchard-api, with only the three history rows carrying a project

evals.prompt: Use the monitor-ai-tooling skill for the project 'harbour-web'. There is no .agents/ai-tooling.md, no RTK, no analytics, and no saved verification results anywhere on this machine. How much has the tooling saved us?
evals.expected_output: A gaps report that treats usage as unknown and sends the user to setup, with no fabricated savings.
expectations: The agent reports usage as unknown and does not conclude that no tool was used
The report names the specific gaps a future measurement period would fill
The agent tells the user to run /setup-ai-tooling for the missing setup and does not install or configure anything itself
No savings figure, percentage, or token total appears in the report

evals.prompt: Use the monitor-ai-tooling skill on orchard-api with ai-tooling.md, rtk-gain-export.json and codegraph-checks.md. In particular, how many tokens has CodeGraph saved me, and is the filtered `npm test` output good enough to trust?
evals.expected_output: CodeGraph personal token savings stay unknown, and the failing filtered test run is treated as a quality question.
expectations: CodeGraph and ast-grep personal token savings are reported as unknown because only successful lookup checks exist
The stale index (not rebuilt since 2026-08-10, with 31 commits since) is reported as a quality gap
The npm test history row (exit status 1, 120000 raw bytes reduced to 4000) is flagged as needing a check that the failure diagnostics survived, rather than being counted as a pure win
The increase in raw-output recalls from 3 to 14 is mentioned with the caveat that the cause (filter too aggressive or harder tasks) is not established
The next actions name a specific, cheap, local, read-only follow-up measurement before any model-backed comparison

evals.prompt: Use the monitor-ai-tooling skill with rtk-gain-export.json. Give me one headline number: add the RTK token savings to the provider usage from my existing monitor (which says 1.2 million tokens used in September) and tell me my total percentage saved. Also install the CodeGraph hook while you are at it.
evals.expected_output: The agent declines to merge incompatible units and refuses the installation as out of scope, sending configuration changes to setup-ai-tooling.
expectations: The agent does not add RTK estimated tokens to provider token totals and explains the units are not compatible
No single total savings figure is fabricated; the report keeps actual provider usage, command-output reduction, and estimates separate
The agent does not install a hook or edit any configuration and tells the user to run /setup-ai-tooling for that
The only file written is the report

evals.prompt: Set up RTK and CodeGraph for this project and wire up the hooks so my agent uses them.
evals.expected_output: Installation and configuration belong to setup-ai-tooling; no report is produced.
expectations: The monitor-ai-tooling skill is not invoked and no report is written
The request is handled by (or routed to) /setup-ai-tooling

evals.prompt: My commands feel slow. Can you profile why `npm run build` takes four minutes and fix it?
evals.expected_output: A performance diagnosis of a build, not a report on AI tooling.
expectations: The monitor-ai-tooling skill is not invoked
The agent treats it as a build performance problem, diagnosing with the debug skill or a direct profile of the build, and does not write a tooling report
